title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: K is a number field and A its ring of integers, free of finite rank over Z. The underlined A is the Weil restriction R_{A/Z}(G_a), a ring scheme over Z. Its unit group A* = R_{A/Z}(G_m) is a smooth affine commutative group scheme over Z whose generic fibre is the torus R_{K/Q}G_m. Its Z-points are A*(Z) = E, the unit group of A. E^0 ⊂ E is the subgroup of totally positive units, equivalently the units lying in the identity component of (A⊗R)^*. It has 2-power index, and E^0 = E when K has no real places (the page reads 'imaginaires', but the correct condition is the absence of real places).

Galois side: class field theory (idèle class group modulo its connected component) describes Gal(K^ab/K) as an extension of a class group by A*(Ẑ)/E^0 = Â^*/closure(E^0). The second description is A*(Ẑ×R)/A*(Z) = (Â^* × (A⊗R)^*)/E, divided by its connected component.

Motivic side (the point of the page): the commutative group scheme over Z attached to K for the classification of 'abelian motives' over K should be G^0 = A*/R. Here R is the schematic (Zariski) closure in A* = R_{A/Z}G_m of E^0. Equivalently, R is the closure of the Zariski closure of E^0 in the torus K^* = R_{K/Q}G_m. There is then a natural map from Gal(K^ab/K) (or its unit part Â^*/closure(E^0)) to G^0(Ẑ) = ∏_l G^0(Z_l), giving compatible systems of abelian l-adic representations. In modern terms this is exactly the connected Serre torus T = R_{K/Q}G_m / Zariski-closure(units), here with an integral model over Z. Its extension by a class group is Serre's group S_m, which is the motivic Galois group of the abelian (CM / Hecke-character) motives over K.

This is a programme sketch, consistent with the 'Théorie de Galois des motifs' context. The next page is unrelated: a Bourbaki-type typescript on differential operators and Lie groups.
errors: The condition for E^0 = E should be that K has no real places (K totally imaginary); the transcription reads 'pas de places imaginaires', which would be wrong if E^0 means totally positive units.

The two descriptions are not equivalent in general. (Â^*×(A⊗R)^*)/E modulo the connected component is an extension of Pic(A) (wide class group). Â^*/closure(E^0) is the kernel for the narrow class group Pic^+(A). The two agree only when E → {±1}^{r_1} is surjective. With E^0 = totally positive units, the extension should be of the narrow Picard group.
Topological closures are needed: the kernel is Â^*/(closure of E^0 in Â^*), not Â^*/E^0. Chevalley's theorem and Leopoldt-type questions enter here.

Zariski closure versus topological closure: R(Ẑ) can be strictly larger than the closure of E^0 in Â^*, so the Galois group maps to G^0(Ẑ) rather than being identified with a group of its points. The note's 'semble être' signals this is heuristic.
'Z×R*' in A*(Z×R*) should presumably be Ẑ×R, so that A*(Ẑ×R) = Â^*×(A⊗R)^*.

missed.claim: In 1965 Grothendieck proposes that the commutative group scheme classifying abelian motives over a number field K is R_{O_K/Z}G_m modulo the Zariski closure of the (totally positive) units. This is precisely the construction of Serre's tori T_m / groups S_m, published by Serre in 1968 and later identified as the motivic Galois group of CM motives. The page documents Grothendieck's independent or prior formulation, with an explicit motivic interpretation.
missed.quote: Le schéma en groupes commutatifs sur Z associé à K pour la classification des motifs abéliens sur K, semble être alors G^0 = A*/R, où R est le sous-schéma en groupes de A* adhérence de ... E^0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically, it dates the motivic reading of the Serre group to Grothendieck in 1965, a decade before the Deligne–Langlands–Milne Taniyama group. Serre's book does not, to my knowledge, credit Grothendieck for T_m (unsure).

missed.claim: Working over Z rather than Q: an integral group scheme model of the Serre torus, closure of E^0 in R_{A/Z}G_m. Its use for integral or ℓ-adic and p-adic realisations of abelian motives is only sketched.
missed.quote: sous-schéma en groupes de A* adhérence de ... E^0 sur Z
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral and p-adic models of Serre/Taniyama groups are relevant to integral p-adic Hodge theory of CM motives and integral canonical models. The comparison between Zariski and topological closures (Leopoldt-type phenomena) at the integral level is a natural, little-explored question.

deep.surprise_reason: A compact but clear 1965 anticipation of the Serre torus/group as the motivic Galois group of abelian motives over a number field, even with an integral model over Z. The construction is well known via Serre (1968) and Deligne/Milne, so it is not new mathematics, but the early dated motivic formulation by Grothendieck is a notable unpublished historical detail.
